title: Corso di Italiano — Livello A0
shortDescription: The SS Europa classroom course, chapter by chapter: start from zero with the same lessons, slides and tests as your teacher. With English and Punjabi.
description:
This is the official SS Europa Italian course used in our classes, for complete beginners from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who are going to Italy to work, study or live.

Each chapter (Capitolo) follows the lessons of the classroom: every 60-minute class is split into three short lessons you can study on your phone, with pictures, audio, grammar tables and exercises. Every word comes with its English and Punjabi meaning, and the slides of each class are attached as PDF. Each chapter ends with a test (pass mark 60%); the written part and the oral interview are done with your teacher.
objectives:

Greet people and introduce yourself: name, city, nationality, age and phone number
Understand the teacher and name the objects of the classroom

Order at the bar and the restaurant, do the shopping and read prices

blocks.title: Le 21 lettere italiane
blocks.body:
The Italian alphabet has **21 letters**: A B C D E F G H I L M N O P Q R S T U V Z.

The letters **J, K, W, X, Y** are "foreign letters" (lettere straniere). They are used only in foreign words such as *jeans*, *kiwi*, *web*, *taxi*, *yoga*.

The 5 vowels (vocali) are **A, E, I, O, U**. In Italian every vowel is always pronounced, and always in the same way.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: A vowel with an accent at the end of a word (**città, caffè, sì, però, più**) is said **strong and clear**, with the voice on the last syllable. The accent can change the meaning: **si** (oneself) / **sì** (yes).

lessons.title: Lesson 1 · Pronunciation: C and G
lessons.summary: Soft and hard C and G: ciao or casa? gelato or gatto?

blocks.title: La lettera C: suono dolce e suono duro
blocks.body:
**C** has two sounds:

- **Soft [ch]** like *church* (Punjabi "ch", chachā) before **E** and **I**: **ce, ci** — and **cia, cio, ciu**.
- **Hard [k]** like *cat* (Punjabi "k", kakkā) before **A, O, U**: **ca, co, cu** — and **che, chi** (the H makes it hard).

blocks.title: La lettera G: suono dolce e suono duro
blocks.body:
**G** works the same way:

- **Soft [j]** like *gel* (Punjabi "j", jajjā): **ge, gi** — and **gia, gio, giu**.
- **Hard [g]** like *go* (Punjabi "g", gaggā): **ga, go, gu** — and **ghe, ghi**.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Remember the trick: **H after C or G makes the sound hard** (chiave, spaghetti). **I after C or G makes it soft** (ciao, giorno) and the I is almost not heard.

blocks.title: Il verbo AVERE (to have · H muta!)

blocks.body:
The **H** of *ho, hai, ha* is silent (muta): **ho** sounds like "o", **ha** like "a".

In Italian you **have** years: *Ho 20 anni* = I am 20 (literally "I have 20 years"). Punjabi: *Merī umar 20 sāl hai*.

blocks.title: Maschile (-O) e femminile (-A)
blocks.body:
Every Italian noun is **masculine** or **feminine**.

- **Masculine** nouns usually end in **-O**: libro, quaderno, tavolo (Pulling: akkhar -O nāl khatam hundā hai)
- **Feminine** nouns usually end in **-A**: penna, sedia, lavagna (Istrīling: akkhar -A nāl khatam hundā hai)

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **Un'** with the apostrophe is only for **feminine** words that start with a vowel (un'aula). Masculine words with a vowel take **un** without apostrophe: *un amico, un orologio*.

blocks.title: Orientarsi sulla piantina (the town map)
blocks.body:
On the map: **Corso Italia** goes north–south, **Via Roma** and **Via Verdi** cross it.

- **Dalla stazione al bar:** vai sempre dritto in Corso Italia — il bar è di fronte alla Piazza Centrale.
- **Dove si trova la posta?** La posta è accanto alla banca e di fronte alla farmacia.
- **Dal parco all'ospedale:** attraversa Piazza Centrale, vai in Via Verdi e gira a destra — è lontano dalla stazione.

3. **Indica la posizione:** vicino a, lontano da, di fronte a, accanto a — poi cambiate ruolo!

blocks.title: Test Capitolo 5
blocks.body:
This test checks everything in Chapter 5 (Lessons 1–4).

- **1. Listening** — sentences and a route through town
- **2. Vocabulary** — city places, directions, rooms and furniture
- **3. Grammar** — andare / venire, prepositions and directions
- **4. Writing** — sentences about your town and your home

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.
